subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the change affects fallback routing, session ownership, provider/model selection, and permission boundaries, so repository policy treats it as a maintainer-owned product/security decision.

options.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime fallback unchanged and add clearer doctor/status/docs guidance for Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair The Linked Fork PR
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source material only after resolving review concerns and proving the behavior in a redacted real Discord setup.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current and historical ownership signal across shared routing, Discord route resolution, and fallback-policy review context.
